run_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full Tessera documentation site, focusing on the primary onboarding flow, reference navigation, interactive controls, and responsive layout states.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed in four phases: validating the homepage onboarding and global controls, navigating the deep reference structure and three-column layouts, testing interactive elements like search and version switching, and finally verifying responsive mobile behavior and layout warnings. The run will prioritize the primary user flow from landing to function reference, while deeply validating high-risk areas like the version switcher and search modal.
assumptions: The version switcher and search modal (⌘K) trigger client-side UI changes without full page reloads.
The left-side TOC tree on reference pages is expandable/collapsible via user interaction.
The 'Get started →' button and quick-start cards likely scroll to sections or link to other pages, despite some prescan `href="#"` values.
The dark/light theme toggle applies a global CSS class to the body or html element.

Search modal (⌘K) interaction and focus trapping
Three-column layout collapse on reference and function detail pages
Small tap targets across navigation and CTAs (especially on mobile)

observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Its clauses are evaluated in a fixed order even though they may be written in any order in the source text. Syntax SELECT [DISTINCT] expression FROM source [WHERE] predicate [GROUP BY] expression [HAVING] predicate [ORDER BY] expression [LIMIT] n [OFFSET] n WITH Common table expressions for readability and recursion. Copy SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://bucket/orders/*.parquet'); WHERE Row-level filter applied before grouping. Supports any expression returning BOOLEAN. GROUP BY Groups rows by the listed expressions. SELECT items must be aggregates or referenced in GROUP BY. HAVING Post-grouping filter, evaluated after aggregates compute. ORDER BY Sorts the final result. Supports ASC / DESC and NULLS FIRST / LAST. LIMIT and OFFSET Restricts the row count. OFFSET can be expensive on large result sets — prefer cursor pagination. Its clauses are evaluated in a fixed order even though they may be written in any order in the source text. Syntax SELECT [DISTINCT] expression FROM source [WHERE] predicate [GROUP BY] expression [HAVING] predicate [ORDER BY] expression [LIMIT] n [OFFSET] n WITH Common table expressions for readability and recursion. Copy WITH recent AS ( SELECT id, amount_cents FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-01' ) SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM recent; FROM Sources can be tables, subqueries, table-valued functions, or external file readers. Copy SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://bucket/orders/*.parquet'); WHERE Row-level filter applied before grouping. Supports any expression returning BOOLEAN. GROUP BY Groups rows by the listed expressions. SELECT items must be aggregates or referenced in GROUP BY. HAVING Post-grouping filter, evaluated after aggregates compute. ORDER BY Sorts the final result. Supports ASC / DESC and NULLS FIRST / LAST. LIMIT and OFFSET Restricts the row count. OFFSET can be expensive on large result sets — prefer cursor pagination. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 v2.4 · 2026-04 release The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics. Tessera runs in your process, reads Parquet and CSV directly, and ships SIMD-optimized vector kernels for sub-millisecond aggregation over millions of rows. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.
